titulo: Kernel prepatch 7.4-rc2
resumo: Linus Torvalds has released the 7.4-rc2 prepatch and it will come as no surprise that it is a large one (" a big -rc2 to go with the largest ever -rc1 "). Much of the size was made up of some automated Coccinelle updates that were spread out all over the tree; once those are factored out, the rest looks fairly normal: When masking that noise out from the diffstat, the shape of it changes - not spread out over thousands of files any more. But it does not look unusual: a third is drivers (gpu, networking and sound account for most of it, but there's a bit of everything), another third is networking and bpf, and the final third is "the rest" (mostly filesystems, mm, arch updates). And yes, much of this was driven by various AI fixes. I think I'll stop repeating that, and we can just take it for granted. But this time around Alexei [Starovoitov] claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true.

titulo: Smart use of trees and crops brings best yield
resumo: Cultivating crops—such as wheat, barley and rye—alongside rows of trees is a system of agroforestry that is known as "alley-cropping." It serves many functions: in addition to enhancing ecosystems and biodiversity, it can also counteract the negative effects of growing crops in treeless open land. The advantages of alley-cropping come from the interaction between trees and crops, resulting in improved soil quality, reduced wind erosion, enhanced nutrient cycling, and climate change mitigation through increased carbon capture.

Sigla em inglês para “Linguagem Comum Orientada para os Negócios”, COBOL é uma linguagem de programação otimizada para processar grandes quantidades de dados. A precisão para lidar com casas decimais e a simplicidade da linguagem fizeram com que o código fosse amplamente usado em sistemas de transações financeiras , como caixas eletrônicos e operações com cartões de crédito ou débito. titulo: Driver da AMD pode desgastar SSD gravando 400 GB de lixo por dia
resumo: Donos de placas de vídeo Radeon : seu PC pode estar sofrendo de um problema silencioso fruto de um bug do driver de vídeo da AMD. O Time Vermelho confirmou o problema em suas versões recentes do driver Radeon Adrenalin, que faz com que um processo do sistema grave dados continuamente no SSD do usuário, mesmo quando a máquina está completamente ociosa . A correção oficial já foi confirmada e chega até o fim de novembro. O problema foi apontado por diversos usuários nas redes sociais, que notaram uma atividade anormal nos discos do sistema . O vilão da história é o processo atieclxx.exe (vinculado ao AMD External Events Utility), serviço responsável por gerenciar atalhos do aplicativo e detecção de monitores. Em sistemas afetados, esse processo mantém uma taxa constante de escrita que varia entre 0,3 MB/s e 1,5 MB/s, com casos mais graves atingindo até 5 MB/s sustentados . O risco à vida útil e como contornar o problema Embora valores na casa dos megabytes por segundo pareçam pequenos à primeira vista, o acúmulo em segundo plano é agressivo. titulo: Can Agentic Robotics Solve Robotics’ Data Scaling Problem?
resumo: Robotics companies are investing heavily in the belief that data will solve the most difficult problems in robotics. Once AI systems have ingested enough data from human demonstrations, the thinking goes, robots will be able to perform the vast majority of the manual tasks that humans now do. There are even robotics companies that exist solely to collect training data and sell it to other robotics companies in pursuit of this goal. But whether data will finally bring us general-purpose robots is an open question . Nobody knows how much data would be necessary , what kind of data is important , or whether something else might be missing . And there are other problems with a reliance on massive amounts of data: the resulting AI algorithms are essentially black boxes, which despite their high performance are difficult or impossible for humans to understand. This characteristic is becoming increasingly concerning in commercial deployments, where robots must be flexible, reliable, and safe. titulo: Sharing a Windows PC? Why you should disable EFS before it’s too late
resumo: Windows’ Encrypted File System (EFS for short) is showing its age. Although it’s still very easy to use – just right-click on a file or folder and select Properties > Advanced > Encrypt contents to protect data – the risk of losing the decryption key is still pretty high. Unlike BitLocker, which encrypts an entire drive, EFS is designed to protect individual files and folders. This can be useful in some situations, but it also means that users may not always be aware of which data they have encrypted. That’s why most folks switched to alternatives like BitLocker, which comes with Windows, or VeraCrypt . The danger with using EFS is that you might encrypt important data, then delete your account and forget to backup the key beforehand. Unfortunately, there’s no way to decrypt data again after that. Especially on company PCs or computers used by multiple people. That’s why we recommend you disable the use of EFS. It reduces the risk of inadvertently encrypting files that could become inaccessible later. Before doing that though, you should check if your files are already encrypted. titulo: Scientists discover a surprising link between acorns and lyme disease
resumo: After more than 35 years of research, scientists have uncovered surprising clues about what really drives Lyme disease risk. Contrary to longstanding assumptions, deer populations appear less important than mice, which can fuel a 40% increase in tick numbers the following year. Even acorn production can predict tick population surges two years in advance, while extreme temperatures may be far less deadly to ticks than scientists once believed.
